children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rose on Monday to finish August with 21.5% price gain as El Nino-related climate woes around the world and high energy prices lifted the market.
New York cocoa also rose to post a 22% monthly price increase, while arabica coffee fell.
There was no trading for robusta coffee, white sugar and London cocoa on Monday due to a bank holiday in England.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
settled up 0.25 cent, or 1.4%, at 17.81 cents per lb.
* Dealers said the market recovered after a large selloff on Friday when prices fell more than 3%.

* "The big question is who sold? One would think it was some spec selling along with some profit taking after a rally of 100 points on the week, coming on the back of a 300 point rally in the preceding three weeks," said sugar analyst and industry advisor Michael McDougall.
* The fundamentals, however, remain mostly supportive, he said, with rains expected in Brazil that could slow down harvesting.
* Archer Consulting said in a note that mills in Brazil could hold on to higher ethanol production for now as prices for the biofuel are recovering.
* On news India expects below-normal September rains after an already weak August, the country's weather department said on Monday.
COCOA
* New York cocoa
​​settled up $123, or 1.9%, to $6,771 a metric ton. The market gained 22% in August.
* Cocoa arrivals at ports in top grower Ivory Coast since October 1 stood at 2 million metric tons by August 30, up 19.6% from the same period last season, exporters estimated on Monday.

* Ivory Coast is expected to keep the fixed price paid to cocoa farmers for their beans at 1,200 CFA francs ($2.14) per kilogram for the 2026/27 main crop season that begins September 1, four industry and two government sources told Reuters.
* "This will likely lead to smuggling out of Ivory Coast as it has occurred in previous years," said StoneX in a note.
COFFEE
* Arabica coffee
settled down 1.35 cent, or 0.4%, at $3.115 per lb. Arabica finished August with a 1% loss.

* Arabica coffee stocks on the ICE exchange fell again on Friday to hit a fresh 26-year low as dealers scrambled for scarce supplies amid concerns the physical market will remain tight in the months ahead.
* Rabobank said in a quarterly coffee report that it still expects a comfortable coffee balance sheet in 2026/27 (Oct-Sept), with a surplus of 8.9 million bags.
* "However, the journey toward a better-supplied market has proved longer and bumpier than previously anticipated," the bank said.
* The market was still digesting a revision of preliminary August coffee export data by Brazilian exporting group Cecafe, which resulted in a large boost on shipments.
